Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck while turning left. Presenting
complaints included neck and low back pain with muscle tension and reduced range of motion. The reported mechanism of injury
is consistent in kind and force with the strain pattern documented on examination. Some findings, including paraspinal muscle
tenderness and limited cervical rotation, support the clinical picture, while other orthopedic and neurological screening tests were
within normal limits. No prior injury to the cervical or lumbar regions is known to this provider or reported in the history.
Conservative care consisted of manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home stretching program. The patient completed 29
visits, a somewhat longer course than typically expected for a strain of this type, with gradual improvement noted over the course
of care. Billing records reviewed for the episode show no duplicate or repeated charges for the same services. At the most recent
evaluation, pain was reduced and function was improving, and the patient was advised to continue the home exercise program as
needed.
